from solution import largest_palindrome


def test_issue_example_given():
    """Example: 'largest palindromic number in the given array' for [1,232,54545,999991] is 54545."""
    assert largest_palindrome([1, 232, 54545, 999991], 4) == 54545  # max(1,232,54545)=54545; 999991 reversed 199999!=999991


def test_issue_single_palindromic_element():
    """'largest palindromic number in the given array' with one element returns that element."""
    assert largest_palindrome([121], 1) == 121  # only candidate 121 reversed 121==121


def test_issue_single_digits_pick_largest():
    """'largest palindromic number' among single digits is the largest digit."""
    assert largest_palindrome([3, 7, 5], 3) == 7  # max(3,7,5)=7; single digits read same


def test_issue_zero_is_palindrome():
    """'largest palindromic number in the given array' treats 0 as a palindrome."""
    assert largest_palindrome([12, 34, 0], 3) == 0  # 12->21 no, 34->43 no, 0->0 yes => 0


def test_issue_skips_non_palindromes():
    """'largest palindromic number in the given array' skips non-palindromes."""
    assert largest_palindrome([123, 456, 11], 3) == 11  # 123->321 no, 456->654 no, 11->11 yes => 11


def test_issue_two_digit_boundary():
    """'largest palindromic number' treats 10 as non-palindrome and 11 and 22 as palindromes."""
    assert largest_palindrome([10, 11, 22], 3) == 22  # max(11,22)=22; 10 reversed 01=1!=10


def test_issue_three_digit_boundary():
    """'largest palindromic number' treats 100 as non-palindrome and 101 as palindrome."""
    assert largest_palindrome([100, 101, 110], 3) == 101  # 100->001=1 no, 110->011=11 no, 101->101 yes => 101


def test_issue_n_limits_to_first_n_elements():
    """'largest palindromic number in the given array' with n considers only the first n elements."""
    assert largest_palindrome([11, 22, 9999], 2) == 22  # max(11,22)=22; 9999 beyond n=2 ignored


def test_issue_largest_in_middle():
    """'largest palindromic number in the given array' is the largest regardless of position."""
    assert largest_palindrome([121, 1331, 99], 3) == 1331  # max(121,1331,99)=1331; all read same reversed


def test_issue_no_palindrome_returns_no_input_value():
    """'largest palindromic number in the given array' with none present must not return a non-palindrome."""
    result = largest_palindrome([12, 34, 56], 3)  # 12->21 no, 34->43 no, 56->65 no => no candidate
    assert result not in (12, 34, 56)  # result 12,34,56 excluded since none is palindrome


def test_contract_result_from_array():
    """'in the given array' means the result must be an element of the array."""
    result = largest_palindrome([121, 123, 131], 3)  # max(121,131)=131; 123 reversed 321!=123
    assert result in (121, 123, 131)  # result must equal one of 121,123,131


def test_contract_result_is_palindrome():
    """'palindromic number' means the result reads the same forward and backward."""
    result = largest_palindrome([123, 232, 454], 3)  # max(232,454)=454; 123 reversed 321!=123
    assert str(result) == str(result)[::-1]  # 454 reversed 454==454 so palindrome holds


def test_contract_input_not_mutated():
    """Function to find the largest palindrome must not modify the given array."""
    a = [121, 123, 131]  # max(121,131)=131; 123 reversed 321!=123
    largest_palindrome(a, 3)  # call should leave input unchanged; expected max=131
    assert a == [121, 123, 131]  # unchanged list equals original literal
